annotations.title: Run an alert in the sandbox

description:
Run one alert through Autoview's Alert Sandbox and see exactly what Autoview would do with it: the parsed orders and a simulated fill for each. No token, no account, no exchange key: simulation only, no real order is placed.

Send the order one of two ways: command (alert text: the classic key=value form "e=kraken s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01" or a v3 line "buy(BTCUSD, 0.01)"), or order (structured: { "exchange": "oanda", "symbol": "EURUSD", "side": "buy", "qty": 1000 }). Not both. A limit order is { ..., "type": "limit", "limit_price": 50000 }. order takes only exchange, symbol, side, qty, type and limit_price: order.price is refused (order_bad_field), because the top-level price is a different thing, the market price you read, not a limit.

Prices. Each fill is priced in this order and labelled with where the price came from (fill.origin): own_key (the user's own connected account; not available yet, coming), venue_ticker (the venue's free public ticker, e.g. Kraken, Coinbase, OKX, Bybit for crypto), caller (a price you pass in price), alert_fp (fp= in the alert, e.g. TradingView {{close}}). If Autoview has no price for the market (stocks, most forex, futures), read the price from your own user's data source and pass it as price (plus price_source and price_time); the fill is then labelled caller-supplied, never presented as Autoview's quote.

Returns { sandbox: true, real_order_placed: false, notice, sandbox_id, webhook_url, compiled?, orders: [{ exchange, side, symbol, qty, type, order_price?, fill }], explanation?, next }.

Fill shapes. A priced fill is { status: "filled", price, price_label, price_source, origin, origin_note, priced_at, price_age_ms, side_of_book?, limit?, price_warning?, caller_price_source?, caller_price_time? }. price_label is Autoview's short label for where the fill price came from, for example "Kraken XBTUSD best ask" (a venue fill at the ask) or "caller-supplied" (your price). price_source is the same label under its older name, kept for existing readers. The source and time you sent with a caller price are echoed in caller_price_source and caller_price_time. A market order, or a limit the book has reached (a buy limit at or above the ask, a sell limit at or below the bid; with a caller price, at or better than it), fills at the ask, bid or your price, never at the limit. price_warning is set when the price was more than 15 minutes old at receipt (for example "The caller price is 5h 2m old"): the fill still used it, so read a fresh price if you want a current fill. A limit the price has not reached is { status: "not_filled", price: null, reference_price, limit, price_label, side_of_book?, origin, origin_note, note, fix }: nothing filled and the sandbox never fills it later; do not pass price again, read fix. An unpriced fill is { status: "no_price", price: null, note, website_note?, price_error? }: price_error is { code, market, message, fix: [steps] }; follow the fix steps and call again.

price_error codes (in fill.price_error, on a no_price fill): no_live_source (Autoview has no live price for this market or venue; pass price, or set e= to a priced crypto venue), venue_read_failed (the venue's public ticker did not answer; retry, or pass price), price_ambiguous (price was sent with an alert that has more than one symbol; send one symbol per call). bad_price_param is the website's code for malformed price fields; it arrives as the refusal bad_price with price_error beside it.

Refusal codes (the whole call returns { error, code, fix }; do what fix says): command_required, command_and_order, bad_v3_line, bad_sandbox_id, order_missing_field, order_bad_field, bad_price, bad_price_source, bad_price_time, price_fields_without_price, sandbox_refused, sandbox_rate_limited, sandbox_bad_answer, sandbox_unreachable, sandbox_timeout, internal_error.

sandbox_id is minted when you omit it; pass it back to add more alerts to the same sandbox, and read them with sandbox_results. Any webhook sender can also POST alerts to webhook_url. Call pricing to see what going live costs.

command.description: alert text, e.g. "e=kraken s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01" (classic key=value) or "buy(BTCUSD, 0.01)" (v3 line). Send this or order, not both

exchange.description: venue id (any spelling) for a v3 line or alert text with no e=, e.g. "kraken"

order.description: structured order (only these six fields; order.price is refused, use limit_price), rendered to the alert line "e=<exchange> s=<symbol> b=<side> q=<qty> t=<type>" (plus fp=<limit_price> for a limit); returned as compiled. Send this or command, not both

exchange.description: venue id, any spelling, e.g. "kraken", "oanda", "alpaca", "coinbase_advanced" (pricing with no exchanges lists every id)

limit_price.description: required when type is "limit": the limit price, e.g. 81000. Not the market price you read: that goes in the top-level price

qty.description: positive quantity in the venue's units, e.g. 0.01 (BTC), 1000 (EUR/USD units), 1 (shares)

symbol.description: one ticker with no spaces, as the venue writes it, e.g. "BTCUSD", "EURUSD", "AAPL"

price.description: optional current market price you read from your own user's data source for this symbol, e.g. 1.11419 or "1.11419" (positive number or decimal string). Used when Autoview has no price for the market; the fill is labelled caller-supplied. Not a limit price: for a limit use order.limit_price (or fp= in command). A price over 15 minutes old still fills, with fill.price_warning

price_source.description: optional, with price: where the price came from, up to 120 characters, e.g. "my OANDA practice account"

price_time.description: optional, with price: when it was read, ISO-8601 ("2026-10-28T17:00:00Z") or epoch milliseconds (1793206684433); not in the future

sandbox_id.description: an existing sandbox id (32 lowercase hex, e.g. "6d43316194e3727e2411ef118974be1f") to reuse; omit to get a new one

name: sandbox_run
